newsitem.title: USA: Edison sets 30-day San Onofre nuke outage next yr.
newsitem.headline: Edison sets 30-day San Onofre nuke outage next yr.

text.p: Southern California Edison Co, a unit of Edison International is planning to shut the 1,087 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the San Onofre nuclear power plant for a 30-day inspection outage next spring, a company spokesman said Thursday.

The mid-cycle outage is part of plans submitted by Edison to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) which is reviewing how to deal with the discovery of erosion of heat transfer tubing within the unit's steam generators, spokesman Ray Golden said.
Unit 3 has been shut for refueling and maintenance since April and Edison still expects to restart the unit on June 26, he noted.
The outage will take place 10 to 12 months after the unit returns to operation, or between next April and June if the unit runs uninterrupted, Golden said.
Earlier this week, Dan Ford, an analyst at HSBC James Capel estimated a mid-cycle outage would cut three to four cents from Edison's 1998 earnings for every month it lasted.
Ford had estimated Edison would earn $1.72 per share next year without an outage.
